changed.title: MacMahon's master theorem as a recurrence for repeated rational permanents (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ) (w : Fin n → ℕ),
  let coeff := fun (v : Fin n → ℕ) =>
    let big : Matrix (Σ j : Fin n, Fin (v j)) (Σ j : Fin n, Fin (v j)) ℚ :=
      fun copyRow copyCol => A copyRow.1 copyCol.1
    big.permanent / (∏ i : Fin n, (Nat.factorial (v i) : ℚ))
  let choices := Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Finset (Fin n) => ∀ t ∈ S, 0 < w t)
  (∑ S ∈ choices, (-1 : ℚ)^S.card *
    (A.submatrix (fun rowIndex : S => rowIndex.val) (fun colIndex : S => colIndex.val)).det *
    coeff (fun pos => w pos - (if pos ∈ S then 1 else 0))) =
    if (∀ t, w t = 0) then 1 else 0
changed.unlocks: Expresses a repeated-index permanent by principal minors and values at smaller multiplicities.
changed.context: Use formal series graded by total degree with B=diag(x)A. The labelled permutation cycle expansion gives the repeated permanent divided by the color factorials as the coefficient in exp(sum over j>0 of trace(B^j)/j). A color-preserving labelling contributes one factorial for each color. Jacobi's derivative identity applied to det(I-tB) shows this series at tB is its inverse, with constant one. Expand the determinant by principal minors and compare the requested coefficient.
changed.sketch: Use formal series graded by total degree with B=diag(x)A. The labelled permutation cycle expansion gives the repeated permanent divided by the color factorials as the coefficient in exp(sum over j>0 of trace(B^j)/j). A color-preserving labelling contributes one factorial for each color. Jacobi's derivative identity applied to det(I-tB) shows this series at tB is its inverse, with constant one. Expand the determinant by principal minors and compare the requested coefficient.

changed.title: The unique furthest configuration of reversible path pebbling at each prescribed number of occupied sites
changed.statement:
∀ (d t : ℕ), t ≤ d →
  let up := fun A B : Finset ℕ => B.card ≤ d ∧
    ∃ i : ℕ, 0 < i ∧ i ∉ A ∧ B = insert i A ∧ (i = 1 ∨ i-1 ∈ A)
  let reach := fun S : Finset ℕ =>
    Relation.ReflTransGen (fun U V => up U V ∨ up V U) ∅ S
  let limit := 2^d - 2^(d-t)
  let extremal := (Finset.range t).image (fun j => 2^d - 2^(d-(j+1)))
  reach extremal ∧ extremal.card = t ∧ extremal.sup id = limit ∧
    ∀ S : Finset ℕ, reach S → S.card = t →
      S.sup id ≤ limit ∧ (S.sup id = limit ↔ S = extremal)
changed.unlocks: characterizes the unique maximally distant reversible path configuration at fixed occupancy
changed.context: With f free pebbles allow deletion across a left gap of at most 2^f. Any eligible deletion may begin a successful clearing order: interchanging two eligible deletions at most doubles the gap while the allowance doubles. Every reachable configuration is clearable. Trace predecessors of its largest position along a clearing order. Their gaps sum to at most 2^(d-t)+...+2^(d-1). Equality uses every stage at equality, forcing the listed positions. To realize them, bridge each gap backwards by recursively reaching its predecessor with the free pebbles.

Any eligible deletion may begin a successful clearing order: interchanging two eligible deletions at most doubles the gap while the allowance doubles. Every reachable configuration is clearable. To realize them, bridge each gap backwards by recursively reaching its predecessor with the free pebbles.

changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 7865809 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 10 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 10 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => (7865809 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: Whether a NOT gate pays under a checked AND/OR floor of 11 on this side-5 graph, by leaving its classes of equal rows or columns unread.
changed.sketch: We hold no circuit of 10 gates; this is a search. This graph has a class of 2 equal columns, which a circuit with NOT gates may leave unread. Give a gate list of AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in two, at most 10 gates, judged by evaluation on the 25 promise inputs. The graph needs at least 11 AND/OR gates by a checked floor row (search 'mask 7865809'). An exhausted search is a report, not a proof.

changed.title: Binary rank gives the exact one-layer nonlinear gate count for fan-in-two circuits on a one-hot table
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD C.output 0
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (u : Fin n) (v : Fin m),
  let entry := fun (a : Fin n) (b : Fin m) => if G a b then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0
  let A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) (ZMod 2) := fun i j =>
    entry i j + entry i v + entry u j + entry u v
  let represents := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C
  ∀ t : ℕ, A.rank ≤ 2*t ↔
    ∃ C, represents C ∧ depth (n+m) C ≤ 1 ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ t
changed.unlocks: determines the exact cost of all one-layer nonlinear selectors from binary anchored rank
changed.context: Every affine wire on two one-hot banks is a row function plus a column function. Expanding a product gives two mixed outer products. The other terms vanish on taking four corners. Sum the rank bounds over the nonlinear gates feeding the output. Conversely factor the anchored matrix into r outer products. Pair ac and bd, where a,b depend on the row and c,d on the column. The gate (a+d)(b+c) gives both after local corrections ab and cd. Pad an odd pair with zero. Every local table is a free XOR lookup. Allow 2 to 4 hours.
changed.sketch: Every affine wire on two one-hot banks is a row function plus a column function. Expanding a product gives two mixed outer products. The other terms vanish on taking four corners. Sum the rank bounds over the nonlinear gates feeding the output. Conversely factor the anchored matrix into r outer products. Pair ac and bd, where a,b depend on the row and c,d on the column. The gate (a+d)(b+c) gives both after local corrections ab and cd. Pad an odd pair with zero. Every local table is a free XOR lookup. Allow 2 to 4 hours.

changed.title: Find a two-product depth-two equality selector on sixteen one-hot names
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD C.output 0
∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack 32 C ∧
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 16 => decide (u = v)) C ∧
  depth 32 C ≤ 2 ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ 2
changed.unlocks: tests whether sixteen-name equality admits two products at depth two
changed.context: Splitting the four name bits into two pairs gives one flat product per pair and one joining AND, three products in all. The anchored rank is fourteen, exactly the two-gate binomial budget, so that bound alone cannot exclude two gates. Try one nested product with independently chosen bank lookups. Test all 256 pairs. We hold no witness meeting this target.

changed.title: Binary Nullstellensatz degree for Horn implications with two endpoints fixed by one allowed pair
changed.statement:
∀ (n d : ℕ) (s t : Fin n), s ≠ t →
  ∀ pred : Fin n → Finset (Fin n), (∀ v, v ≠ s → v ∉ pred v) →
  let P := MvPolynomial (Fin n) (ZMod 2)
  let static := fun (axioms : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) (budget : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (q : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n) → P) (b : Fin n → P),
      (∀ C ∈ axioms, q C = 0 ∨ (q C).totalDegree + (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly C).totalDegree ≤ budget) ∧
      (∀ v, b v = 0 ∨ (b v).totalDegree + 2 ≤ budget) ∧
      axioms.sum (fun C => q C * PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly C) +
        (∑ v, b v * (MvPolynomial.X v * MvPolynomial.X v + MvPolynomial.X v)) = 1
  let clause := fun v : Fin n =>
    insert (v,true) ((pred v).image (fun u => (u,false)))
  let pins : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)) :=
    {{(t,true),(s,true)}, {(t,false),(s,true)}, {(t,false),(s,false)}}
  let F := (Finset.univ.erase s).image clause ∪ pins
  let enabled := fun (z : Option (Fin n)) (current : Finset (Option (Fin n))) =>
    z = none ∨ ∃ i : Fin n, z = some i ∧
      ((i = s ∧ none ∈ current) ∨ (i ≠ s ∧ ∀ u ∈ pred i, some u ∈ current))
  let up := fun A B : Finset (Option (Fin n)) => B.card ≤ d ∧
    ∃ z, z ∉ A ∧ B = insert z A ∧ enabled z A
  static F d ↔
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), t ∈ S ∧ (S.card < d ∨ s ∈ S) ∧
      Relation.ReflTransGen (fun U V => up U V ∨ up V U) ∅ (S.image some)
changed.unlocks: converts a static refutation with a paired source and sink into a terminal pebbling and conversely
changed.context: Expand each bounded-degree cofactor in monomials and take squarefree supports on the cube. Interior rules toggle a vertex with its parents present. For any external support of size at most d-2, the three endpoint polynomials span a source toggle and the two sink monomials, with or without the source. One extra predecessor enforces the lost source slot. The empty component must meet an allowable sink monomial. Conversely sum the formal edge identities along a path and add its terminal monomial. The budget permits all cofactors.
changed.sketch: Expand each bounded-degree cofactor in monomials and take squarefree supports on the cube. Interior rules toggle a vertex with its parents present. For any external support of size at most d-2, the three endpoint polynomials span a source toggle and the two sink monomials, with or without the source. One extra predecessor enforces the lost source slot. The empty component must meet an allowable sink monomial. Conversely sum the formal edge identities along a path and add its terminal monomial. The budget permits all cofactors.

changed.title: The Boyar-Find bound on nonlinearity in terms of the AND count of a Boolean circuit (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ n : ℕ,
  let V := Fin n → ZMod 2
  let admissible := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack n C ∧
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates,
      (g.op = .and ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) ∨
      (g.op = .mod 2 ∧ g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∨
      (g.op = .not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1))
  let cost := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    C.gates.countP (fun g => @decide (g.op = .and) (Classical.propDecidable _))
  let input := fun (x : V) => List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => decide (x i = 1))
  ∀ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (f : V → ZMod 2),
    admissible C → (∀ x : V, C.eval (input x) = decide (f x = 1)) →
    ∃ (a : V) (b : ZMod 2),
      2*((Finset.univ : Finset V).filter (fun z => f z ≠ dotProduct a z + b)).card + 2^(n - cost C) ≤ 2^n
changed.unlocks: Lower-bounds nested AND complexity from the distance of a Boolean table to all affine functions.
changed.context: Boyar and Find, Proposition 2. Combine the affine restriction through the ANDs with the bound on affine distance. Estimated proof time 1 to 2 hours after 501 and 502.
changed.sketch: On paper. Cut one affine operand at each AND as needed to leave a flat of dimension at least n−s on which the output is affine. Average affine extensions of that restriction. All points of the flat agree and the mean off-flat agreement is one half. This also works for s≥n, when keeping a single point suffices.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 272380 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 11 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 6) => (272380 : ℕ).testBit (6 * u.val + v.val)) 11
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 6 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 12 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out, equal gates merged and unread gates dropped); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 11; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 9 (on paper), a gap of 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 9 right, gate j writes wire 10 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 24 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. Inequivalent weighted automata have a distinguishing word shorter than their combined dimension
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (q d e : ℕ),
  let V := Fin d → K
  let W := Fin e → K
  ∀ (s : V) (t : W) (A : Fin q → V →ₗ[K] V) (B : Fin q → W →ₗ[K] W)
    (f : V →ₗ[K] K) (g : W →ₗ[K] K),
    let X := fun (w : List (Fin q)) => w.foldl (fun x a => A a x) s
    let Y := fun (w : List (Fin q)) => w.foldl (fun y a => B a y) t
    (∃ w, f (X w) ≠ g (Y w)) →
      ∃ w, w.length < d + e ∧ f (X w) ≠ g (Y w)
changed.unlocks: bounds a distinguishing input length by the combined state dimension
changed.context: Run both systems in the direct sum and subtract their terminal functionals. Its dimension is d+e. A basis of reachable states is generated by words shorter than d+e. If the difference vanishes on every basis vector, linearity makes it vanish on every word. This also handles a zero-dimensional system.
changed.sketch: Run both systems in the direct sum and subtract their terminal functionals. Its dimension is d+e. A basis of reachable states is generated by words shorter than d+e. If the difference vanishes on every basis vector, linearity makes it vanish on every word. This also handles a zero-dimensional system.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. Equivalent minimal weighted automata are related by a unique intertwining change of basis
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (q d e : ℕ),
  let V := Fin d → K
  let W := Fin e → K
  ∀ (s : V) (t : W) (A : Fin q → V →ₗ[K] V) (B : Fin q → W →ₗ[K] W)
    (f : V →ₗ[K] K) (g : W →ₗ[K] K),
    let X := fun (w : List (Fin q)) => w.foldl (fun x a => A a x) s
    let Y := fun (w : List (Fin q)) => w.foldl (fun y a => B a y) t
    Submodule.span K (Set.range X) = ⊤ →
    Submodule.span K (Set.range Y) = ⊤ →
    (∀ x : V, (∀ w : List (Fin q), f (w.foldl (fun y a => A a y) x) = 0) → x = 0) →
    (∀ y : W, (∀ w : List (Fin q), g (w.foldl (fun x a => B a x) y) = 0) → y = 0) →
    (∀ w, f (X w) = g (Y w)) →
    ∃! H : V ≃ₗ[K] W, H s = t ∧ (∀ x, g (H x) = f x) ∧
      ∀ (a : Fin q) (x : V), H (A a x) = B a (H x)
changed.unlocks: relates minimal realizations by a unique invertible linear map
changed.context: Send the state reached by each word to the corresponding state in the second system. Any linear relation among reached states gives zero under all future output functionals. Equality on concatenations transfers the relation, and observability in the second system makes it a vector relation. Extend linearly by reachability. Reverse the roles to obtain the inverse. Agreement on all reached vectors forces uniqueness.
changed.sketch: Send the state reached by each word to the corresponding state in the second system. Any linear relation among reached states gives zero under all future output functionals. Equality on concatenations transfers the relation, and observability in the second system makes it a vector relation. Extend linearly by reachability. Reverse the roles to obtain the inverse. Agreement on all reached vectors forces uniqueness.
